question: Which Indian Billiard player won his 28th World Billiards Title at IBSF World Billiards Championship in Doha, Qatar in November 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pankaj Advani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pankaj Advani is an Indian professional billiards and snooker player, widely regarded as one of the best cue sports players in history.
 
• He won his 28th World Billiards Title at the IBSF World Billiards Championship held in Doha, Qatar in November 2024.
 
• Advani is known for his dominance in both the short format (150-up) and the long format (points) of billiards.
 
• With this victory, he further cemented his legacy as the most successful cueist in the history of the sport.
 
• He holds multiple titles in both billiards and snooker at the national and international levels, showcasing his versatility and skill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IBSF World Billiards Championship:**

 
 
• The International Billiards and Snooker Federation (IBSF) organizes the World Billiards Championship annually.
 
• This championship features two formats – points format and timed format – which test players' strategy and endurance.
 
• It serves as one of the most prestigious tournaments in the world of billiards.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of Pankaj Advani:**
 
 
• Advani has won multiple World Championships across different formats in billiards and snooker.
 
• He is a recipient of India's highest sporting honors, including the Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri, and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award.
 
• His contributions have significantly elevated the profile of cue sports in India.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Billiards and Snooker:**
 
 
• Billiards is typically played with three balls (cue ball, red ball, and opponent's cue ball) on a table with no pockets.
 
• Snooker uses 21 balls, including a cue ball and 15 red balls, played on a table with six pockets.
 
• The scoring systems and rules vary significantly between the two sports.
 
 
 
• **India's Legacy in Cue Sports:**
 
 
• India has produced legendary players like Wilson Jones, Michael Ferreira, and Geet Sethi, apart from Pankaj Advani.
 
• Indian players have consistently excelled in international championships, earning the country global recognition in billiards and snooker.
